reason: E2 shows GDML can learn accurate force fields from few AIMD samples for small molecules, but not for high-entropy alloys. E1 describes UI methodology but not with an ML surrogate. E3 uses covariance-based entropy for solids but E4 warns the Gaussian approximation may fail for large displacements, which are expected near melting. No evidence supports the claimed speedups or active learning for this context.
premises: ML surrogates trained on AIMD data can accurately reproduce ab initio potential energy surfaces for high-entropy alloys.
Active learning can efficiently refine the ML surrogate in regions of high free energy gradients.
Umbrella integration (UI) with an ML surrogate can yield accurate free energy profiles.
Covariance-based vibrational entropy extraction from MD trajectories is valid for high-entropy alloys near melting.
The combined ML+UI+covariance approach reduces cost by ~10x vs. explicit AIMD and 3-5x vs. TOR-TILD.
